lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Hey Gary, Yolanda here. How's your Tuesday going?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Hi, yes, perfect timing.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Great. So today I'd like to hear how the walks after dinner went, check how you're feeling, and pick a goal for next week. Anything you want to add?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Sounds good to me.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What happened with the walks after dinner?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I didn't do it. I'm just so tired, I don't have it in me.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: How do you want to handle the walks after dinner going forward?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Maybe after the summer.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Is that something you can do?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: No, not really. I'm just so tired, I don't have it in me.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: How would things be different if you kept this up?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I've always eaten late, that's how we do it at home.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Would it be okay if I shared something that's helped other people?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Go ahead.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: A short walk after dinner, even 10 minutes, really helps bring blood sugar down.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'm too tired for this right now.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Do you eat dinner at the same time every day?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yes. Between appointments and everything, there was no time.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Can I share an idea?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Sure.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: A short walk after dinner, even 10 minutes, really helps bring blood sugar down.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Mm-hmm.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: My health is why I'm doing this. My daughter keeps reminding me.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You've noticed it makes a difference.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Maybe.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What do you think the next step should be?

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Right.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'm going to do it Monday, Wednesday and Friday.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You already did the hardest part, which is starting.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Walking hurts my knees, so why bother.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Could someone in the family walk with you?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah, I think so. I don't know where the day goes.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: The days got away from you.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I don't know.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Whatever you pick is fine with me. It's your plan.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're open to it. You just want it to fit your real life.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Mm-hmm.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Well, my family eats late, like at 9, and I'm not going to eat alone. Church on Sunday always throws me off.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What did you notice on the days it went well?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: My sugar is lower in the morning when I walk after dinner.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You know your schedule better than anyone.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What could you try instead?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I have to do something, I don't want the cancer back.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Part of you is already moving, and you want to keep that going.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'll set an alarm on my phone.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You've made up your mind.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Mm-hmm.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: It rained almost every afternoon.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: How do you want to handle the walks after dinner going forward?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Okay, this week I'll really do it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What feels doable for next week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'll try to take a 10-minute walk after dinner on 4 days.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: It's completely your call.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: On a scale of 0 to 10, how confident are you that you can do that?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: 5. Maybe 6.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Why a 5 and not a 2?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I feel better about myself when I stick to it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: If the rain gets in the way again, what's your backup plan?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'll ask my son to come with me.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Let me make sure I got it. This week you did it 0 out of 5 days, the hard part was being so tired, and next week you're going to take a 10-minute walk after dinner on 4 days. Did I miss anything?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah, and I'll really try this time.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: I'll text you midweek to see how it's going, and we'll talk again in two weeks.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: That works.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Talk soon!

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Thanks, bye bye.

tags.note: Repeats advice already rejected; permission not re-asked
Praise for starting, though he reported no walks yet
Repeats question from line 7 without engaging rain barrier

flags.reason: Repeats the same walking advice verbatim after the participant rejected it, without new permission or engagement with his fatigue and knee pain.
Re-asks the handling question from line 7 after the participant already answered, ignoring the rain barrier he raised at line 49.
Agenda promised a check on how he is feeling, but that step never occurs in the call.

score.summary: Yolanda reflected some of Gary's change talk and built a concrete goal (10-minute walks on 4 days) with a backup plan, but she repeated advice after he pushed back and never checked his feelings as promised. Gary's fatigue and knee pain were not explored, so the plan rests on his effort more than on his own barrier-solving.
strengths: Line 36 complex reflection captured his openness and wish for a plan that fits real life.
Line 41 affirmed his knowledge of his own schedule, which supported his autonomy.
Line 59 planned for the rain barrier with an open backup-plan question, and line 61 summarized the plan clearly.
coaching_tips: Line 21 repeated the rejected advice word for word; ask permission again or reflect the fatigue first.
Line 50 re-asked a question already answered at line 8; reflect the rain barrier from line 49 instead.
Line 3 promised to check feelings but this never happened; ask how he feels before moving to goals.
Line 29 praised starting, but he had not walked yet; affirm the effort he actually made, such as attending today's call.
Line 30 knee pain was a real barrier; explore it with an open question before offering suggestions.
